subsection.title: Solve Proportions
subsection.p: When two rational expressions are equal, the equation relating them is called a proportion.

note.p: A proportion is an equation of the form $$\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d}$$, where $$b \neq 0,d \neq 0$$.
The proportion is read “$$a$$ is to $$b$$, as $$c$$ is to $$d$$.”

subsection.p: The equation $$\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{8}$$ is a proportion because the two fractions are equal. The proportion $$\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{8}$$ is read “1 is to 2 as 4 is to 8.”

Proportions are used in many applications to ‘scale up’ quantities. We’ll start with a very simple example so you can see how proportions work. Even if you can figure out the answer to the example right away, make sure you also learn to solve it using proportions.

Suppose a school principal wants to have 1 teacher for 20 students. She could use proportions to find the number of teachers for 60 students. We let x be the number of teachers for 60 students and then set up the proportion:
We are careful to match the units of the numerators and the units of the denominators—teachers in the numerators, students in the denominators.

Since a proportion is an equation with rational expressions, we will solve proportions the same way we solved equations in Solve Rational Equations. We’ll multiply both sides of the equation by the LCD to clear the fractions and then solve the resulting equation.
So let’s finish solving the principal’s problem now. We will omit writing the units until the last step.

row.cell: Multiply both sides by the LCD, 60.
The principal needs 3 teachers for 60 students.

subsection.p: Now we’ll do a few examples of solving numerical proportions without any units. Then we will solve applications using proportions.

subsection.p: To solve applications with proportions, we will follow our usual strategy for solving applications. But when we set up the proportion, we must make sure to have the units correct—the units in the numerators must match and the units in the denominators must match.

problem.p: When pediatricians prescribe acetaminophen to children, they prescribe 5 milliliters (ml) of acetaminophen for every 25 pounds of the child’s weight. If Zoe weighs 80 pounds, how many milliliters of acetaminophen will her doctor prescribe?

row.cell: Identify what we are asked to find, and choose a variable to represent it.
How many ml of acetaminophen will the doctor prescribe?
Write a sentence that gives the information to find it.
If 5 ml is prescribed for every 25 pounds, how much will be prescribed for 80 pounds?
Translate into a proportion–be careful of the units.$$\frac{\text{ml}}{\text{pounds}} = \frac{\text{ml}}{\text{pounds}}$$
Multiply both sides by the LCD, 400.
Remove common factors on each side.
Simplify, but don't multiply on the left. Notice what the next step will be.
Yes, since 80 is about 3 times 25, the medicine should be about 3 times 5. So 16 ml makes sense.
The pediatrician would prescribe 16 ml of acetaminophen to Zoe.

note.p: Pediatricians prescribe 5 milliliters (ml) of acetaminophen for every 25 pounds of a child’s weight. How many milliliters of acetaminophen will the doctor prescribe for Emilia, who weighs 60 pounds?

For every 1 kilogram (kg) of a child’s weight, pediatricians prescribe 15 milligrams (mg) of a fever reducer. If Isabella weighs 12 kg, how many milligrams of the fever reducer will the pediatrician prescribe?

problem.p: A 16-ounce iced caramel macchiato has 230 calories. How many calories are there in a 24-ounce iced caramel macchiato?

row.cell: Identify what we are asked to find, and choose a variable to represent it.
How many calories are in a 24 ounce iced caramel macchiato?
Write a sentence that gives the information to find it.
If there are 230 calories in 16 ounces, then how many calories are in 24 ounces?
Translate into a proportion–be careful of the units.$$\frac{\text{calories}}{\text{ounce}} = \frac{\text{calories}}{\text{ounce}}$$
Multiply both sides by the LCD, 48.
Remove common factors on each side.
Yes, 345 calories for 24 ounces is more than 290 calories for 16 ounces, but not too much more.
There are 345 calories in a 24-ounce iced caramel macchiato.

note.p: At a fast-food restaurant, a 22-ounce chocolate shake has 850 calories. How many calories are in their 12-ounce chocolate shake? Round your answer to nearest whole number.
Yaneli loves Starburst candies, but wants to keep her snacks to 100 calories. If the candies have 160 calories for 8 pieces, how many pieces can she have in her snack?

problem.p: Josiah went to Mexico for spring break and changed $325 dollars into Mexican pesos. At that time, the exchange rate had $1 US is equal to 12.54 Mexican pesos. How many Mexican pesos did he get for his trip?

row.cell: What are you asked to find?
How many Mexican pesos did Josiah get?
Write a sentence that gives the information to find it.
If $1 US is equal to 12.54 Mexican pesos, then $325 is how many pesos?
Translate into a proportion–be careful of the units.
Multiply both sides by the LCD, $$12.54p$$.
Remove common factors on each side.
Yes, $100 would be 1,254 pesos. $325 is a little more than 3 times this amount, so our answer of 4075.5 pesos makes sense.
Josiah got 4075.5 pesos for his spring break trip.

note.p: Yurianna is going to Europe and wants to change $800 dollars into Euros. At the current exchange rate, $1 US is equal to 0.738 Euro. How many Euros will she have for her trip?
Corey and Nicole are traveling to Japan and need to exchange $600 into Japanese yen. If each dollar is 94.1 yen, how many yen will they get?

subsection.p: In the example above, we related the number of pesos to the number of dollars by using a proportion. We could say the number of pesos is proportional to the number of dollars. If two quantities are related by a proportion, we say that they are proportional.

subsection.title: Solve Similar Figure Applications
subsection.p: When you shrink or enlarge a photo on a phone or tablet, figure out a distance on a map, or use a pattern to build a bookcase or sew a dress, you are working with similar figures. If two figures have exactly the same shape, but different sizes, they are said to be similar. One is a scale model of the other. All their corresponding angles have the same measures and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

note.p: Two figures are similar if the measures of their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

subsection.p: For example, the two triangles in Figure 8.2 are similar. Each side of $$\text{Δ}ABC$$ is 4 times the length of the corresponding side of $$\text{Δ}XYZ$$.

image.alt: Diagram of two triangles, ABC and XYZ. Triangle ABC has side lengths AB equal to 12, BC equal to 16, and AC equal to 20. Triangle XYZ has side lengths XY equal to 3, YZ equal to 4, and XZ equal to 5. The image indicates that angle A is congruent to angle X, angle B is congruent to angle Y, and angle C is congruent to angle Z. Ratios of corresponding sides are shown: AB/XY equals 12/3, BC/YZ equals 16/4, and AC/XZ equals 20/5.

subsection.p: This is summed up in the Property of Similar Triangles.

note.p: If $$\text{Δ}ABC$$ is similar to $$\text{Δ}XYZ$$, then their corresponding angle measure are equal and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

subsection.p: To solve applications with similar figures we will follow the Problem-Solving Strategy for Geometry Applications we used earlier.

list.item: Step 1. Read the problem and make all the words and ideas are understood. Draw the figure and label it with the given information.
Step 2. Identify what we are looking for.
Step 3. Name what we are looking for by choosing a variable to represent it.
Step 4. Translate into an equation by writing the appropriate formula or model for the situation. Substitute in the given information.
Step 5. Solve the equation using good algebra techniques.
Step 6. Check the answer in the problem and make sure it makes sense.
Step 7. Answer the question with a complete sentence.

problem.p: $$\text{Δ}ABC$$ is similar to $$\text{Δ}XYZ$$. The lengths of two sides of each triangle are given. Find the lengths of the third sides.

row.cell: Step 1. Read the problem. Draw the figure and label it with the given information.
Step 2. Identify what we are looking for.
the length of the sides of similar triangles
Let $$\; a =$$ length of the third side of $$\text{Δ}ABC.$$ $$y =$$ length of the third side of $$\text{Δ}XYZ$$
Since the triangles are similar, the corresponding sides are proportional.

We need to write an equation that compares the side we are looking for to a known ratio. Since the side AB = 4 corresponds to the side XY = 3 we know $$\frac{AB}{XY} = \frac{4}{3}$$. So we write equations with $$\frac{AB}{XY}$$ to find the sides we are looking for. Be careful to match up corresponding sides correctly.
The third side of $$\text{Δ}ABC$$ is 6 and the third side of $$\text{Δ}XYZ$$ is 2.4.

note.p: $$\text{Δ}ABC$$ is similar to $$\text{Δ}XYZ$$. The lengths of two sides of each triangle are given in the figure.
Find the length of side $$a$$.
$$\text{Δ}ABC$$ is similar to $$\text{Δ}XYZ$$. The lengths of two sides of each triangle are given in the figure.
Find the length of side $$y$$.

subsection.p: The next example shows how similar triangles are used with maps.

problem.p: On a map, San Francisco, Las Vegas, and Los Angeles form a triangle whose sides are shown in the figure below. If the actual distance from Los Angeles to Las Vegas is 270 miles find the distance from Los Angeles to San Francisco.

row.cell: Read the problem. Draw the figures and label with the given information.
Identify what we are looking for.
The actual distance from Los Angeles to San Francisco.
Let $$x =$$ distance from Los Angeles to San Francisco.
Translate into an equation. Since the trianglesare similar, the corresponding sides areproportional. We'll make the numerators"miles" and the denominators "inches."
On the map, the distance from Los Angeles toSan Francisco is more than the distance fromLos Angeles to Las Vegas. Since 351 is morethan 270 the answer makes sense.
The distance from Los Angeles to San Francisco is 351 miles.

subsection.p: We can use similar figures to find heights that we cannot directly measure.

problem.p: Tyler is 6 feet tall. Late one afternoon, his shadow was 8 feet long. At the same time, the shadow of a tree was 24 feet long. Find the height of the tree.

row.cell: Read the problem and draw a figure.
We are looking for h, the height of the tree.
We will use similar triangles to write an equation.
The small triangle is similar to the large triangle.
Tyler's height is less than his shadow's length so it makessense that the tree's height is less than the length of its shadow.

note.p: A telephone pole casts a shadow that is 50 feet long. Nearby, an 8 foot tall traffic sign casts a shadow that is 10 feet long. How tall is the telephone pole?
A pine tree casts a shadow of 80 feet next to a 30-foot tall building which casts a 40 feet shadow. How tall is the pine tree?
